topic: The warship that sank because nobody dared tell the king — Vasa, 1628

through_line.name: A single gilded lion-head gun port lid
through_line.progression: Introduced as a corroded relic in the cold open, then followed forward from raw lime log to carved face to gilded lid to the hatch that is deliberately opened for a ceremonial salute — the exact hole the sea comes through. It sinks with the ship, is sealed in silt, and is lifted again in 1961.
through_line.resolution: The same lid, gold still legible, lit under museum glass in the payoff — the object that killed the ship is the object that made her famous.

blocks.vo_line: She was the most powerful warship in Europe. She sailed thirteen hundred metres, rolled onto her side and sank, with every man aboard already knowing she would.
blocks.through_line_state: Corroded and half-buried in silt, gold leaf flaking off the lion's face.
shots: ECU low — the lion lid's blind gilded eye in green dark, silt drifting across it
WIDE high — the whole wreck on the seabed, masts snapped, scale bar of light from above
MEDIUM lateral — a row of open gun ports like missing teeth along the hull
CU overhead — a bronze cannon muzzle furred with sediment
WIDE low — the hull's carved stern rising into black water, gold catching one shaft of light

blocks.vo_line: Stockholm, sixteen twenty-five: Sweden is eleven years into a war that will last thirty. King Gustavus Adolphus wants a navy built to frighten every rival on the Baltic.
blocks.through_line_state: A chalk sketch of the lion face lies on the corner of the campaign table.
shots: MEDIUM lateral — candlelit campaign table, a map of the Baltic weighted with shot
CU overhead — the king's hand dragging a marker across the map
WIDE low — the tent interior, banners, officers standing back in shadow
ECU — the chalk lion sketch at the table's edge, half under a dispatch
MEDIUM high — the map from above, Sweden ringed, the sea empty of ships

blocks.vo_line: He orders four ships, and the largest will carry his own family name: Vasa. Sixty-nine metres of oak, ten sails, more carved gold than any hull in Europe.
blocks.through_line_state: The lid count is written into the specification sheet for the first time.
shots: CU lateral — a quill signing the contract, wax seal pressed
MEDIUM low — the king turning from the table, back to camera
ECU overhead — the spec sheet, a column of numbers, the lid count circled
WIDE lateral — a courier taking the sealed order out through the tent flap
MEDIUM high — the order travelling: a rider, then a sail, then a quay

blocks.vo_line: A thousand oaks come down for her, and the shipwrights work entirely by eye. Nobody has drawings, calculations, or any reliable way to predict what actually floats.
blocks.through_line_state: A raw lime log is set aside — the blank the lion will be cut from.
shots: WIDE high — a felled oak forest, stumps in rows, logs dragged by oxen
CU lateral — a two-man sawpit, blade biting, sawdust falling
ECU — a shipwright's thumb held up against a curved rib, measuring by eye
MEDIUM low — the raw lime log leaning alone against a fence
WIDE lateral — the timber yard entire, stacks receding into fog

blocks.vo_line: The master shipwright is Henrik Hybertsson: Dutch, experienced, and dying. He falls ill in sixteen twenty-six, never sees the keel finished, and leaves his young assistant the entire project.
blocks.through_line_state: The lion is roughed out — a blank muzzle, no face yet.
shots: MEDIUM lateral — the master shipwright coughing over a plan he cannot finish
CU high — his hands going still on the timber
ECU — the roughed-out lion blank, chisel marks, no eyes
MEDIUM low — Jakobsson in the doorway, being handed the ledger
WIDE high — the empty keel in its cradle, scaffolding half-built around it

blocks.vo_line: Hein Jakobsson has never designed a warship alone. He also has a king writing letters from a battlefield in Prussia, asking why the ship is not finished yet.
blocks.through_line_state: Unfinished lids stack up in the yard, faces still blank.
shots: MEDIUM lateral — Jakobsson alone at a trestle, ledger open, nothing written
ECU overhead — an unopened letter with a broken royal seal
WIDE low — the growing hull in its cradle, ribs like a ribcage
CU high — a stack of blank lion lids under a tarpaulin
MEDIUM low — Jakobsson looking up at the hull, dwarfed by it

blocks.vo_line: Then the king changes the specification: a second gun deck, sixty-four bronze cannon instead of thirty-six. The hull is already built, and the keel cannot be widened.
blocks.through_line_state: The required lid count doubles — struck out and rewritten on the spec sheet.
shots: ECU overhead — the number thirty-six struck through, sixty-four written above it
MEDIUM lateral — the king dictating, not looking up
WIDE high — a diagram of the hull gaining a whole second row of ports
CU low — Jakobsson reading the revision, jaw set
MEDIUM high — the keel from above, unchanged and unchangeable

blocks.vo_line: Two decks of guns means enormous weight high above the waterline, where every tonne pushes sideways on the mast. Nobody in Sweden can yet calculate that force.
blocks.through_line_state: A finished lid is held up against the hull to check the fit.
shots: WIDE lateral — the lower gun deck, a corridor of cannon vanishing aft
CU low — a cannon's trunnion settling into its carriage, timber flexing
ECU — a plumb line hanging, swinging, refusing to settle
MEDIUM high — a lid offered up to an empty port, light behind it
WIDE low — the upper gun deck directly above, doubling the same weight

blocks.vo_line: The bronze guns alone weigh over seventy tonnes. They sit behind hatches cut low in the hull, each one sealed by a lid carved as a gilded lion's head.
blocks.through_line_state: First complete lid: mounted in its port, hinged, closed.
shots: ECU lateral — the lid swinging shut, the lion's face arriving in frame
MEDIUM low — a gun crew heaving a bronze barrel into position
CU overhead — the hinge pin driven home with a mallet
WIDE lateral — a row of closed lion lids down the hull's inside
MEDIUM high — the same row seen from outside the hull, gold against black tar

blocks.vo_line: Roughly seven hundred sculptures are carved for her: emperors, mermaids, warriors, lions, painted in twenty colours and gilded. This ship is not a weapon, it is an argument.
blocks.through_line_state: The lid is gilded — gold leaf laid on and burnished until it glows.
shots: WIDE high — the carving shop, benches crowded with half-finished figures
ECU — gold leaf lifted on a brush and laid onto the lion's brow
CU lateral — a mermaid's face emerging under a gouge
MEDIUM low — pigment pots in twenty colours, ranked on a shelf
WIDE lateral — finished sculptures crated and stacked to the roof

blocks.vo_line: Every carving is oak and lime, and every carving sits above the waterline. The propaganda that makes her terrifying is the same propaganda that makes her top-heavy.
blocks.through_line_state: The lid is weighed — the scale pan drops hard.
shots: CU overhead — the gilded lid dropped onto a scale pan, the beam slamming down
MEDIUM lateral — crates of carvings being hoisted upward, always upward
ECU low — a chalked waterline on the hull, every sculpture above it
WIDE low — the stern castle rising, tier on tier of gold
MEDIUM high — the ship in profile, the top half visibly heavier than the bottom

blocks.vo_line: Down in the hold they load one hundred and twenty tonnes of stone as ballast, and it is not enough. There is no room for more without flooding the lower deck.
blocks.through_line_state: Weighed against a ballast stone — the lid wins.
shots: WIDE low — the hold, lantern-lit, men passing stones hand to hand
ECU — a granite ballast stone dropped onto the pile, dust jumping
CU high — bilge water already licking the top of the stone bed
MEDIUM lateral — a man measuring the remaining gap with his forearm: none
WIDE high — the hold from the hatch above, full to the beams

blocks.vo_line: That is the trap: add ballast and the lower gun ports sink toward the sea. Leave it out, and she stands far too tall to survive a strong breeze.
blocks.through_line_state: A waterline is chalked on the hull — the lid sits barely above it.
shots: ECU lateral — a chalk line drawn along the hull's inside, just under a port
MEDIUM low — the same port from inside, the lid a hand's width above the mark
CU overhead — a diagram: stones down, ports down; stones out, mast tips
WIDE lateral — the hold and the gun deck stacked in one cutaway frame
MEDIUM high — the chalk line, wiped away by a passing shoulder

blocks.vo_line: By the summer of sixteen twenty-eight she is finished, moored at the palace quay, and she is genuinely magnificent. She is also the tallest, narrowest mistake in the Baltic.
blocks.through_line_state: Gleaming, closed, flawless — polished for display.
shots: WIDE low — the finished ship at the quay, ten sails furled, gold everywhere
ECU — the lion lid polished to a mirror, a cloth withdrawing from frame
MEDIUM lateral — citizens on the quay stopping to stare upward
CU high — the masts from the deck, absurdly tall against cloud
WIDE high — the ship from above, narrow as a blade, top-heavy as a wedding cake

blocks.vo_line: In August, Vice-Admiral Klas Fleming comes aboard to run the standard stability trial. Thirty men are ordered to run together from one rail to the other and back.
blocks.through_line_state: Closed and dry as the test begins.
shots: MEDIUM low — Fleming crossing the quay toward the gangplank, coat, gorget, unreadable face
WIDE lateral — thirty men mustering on the stones below the hull
ECU — the closed lion lid at eye level as the men file past it
CU high — boots going up the gangplank in sequence
MEDIUM high — the quay emptying as the last man boards

blocks.vo_line: They manage three runs. On the third the ship heels so far that Fleming stops the test, because he can see she is about to roll over at anchor.
blocks.through_line_state: The lid dips toward the water as she heels — closer than it has ever been.
shots: WIDE low — the deck canting hard, horizon swinging up out of frame
ECU — the lion lid swinging down toward the water, its reflection rising to meet it
CU lateral — Fleming's hand going up: stop
MEDIUM high — the men frozen mid-deck, gripping the rail, no one speaking
WIDE lateral — the ship rocking back upright, slowly, too slowly

blocks.vo_line: This is the moment the disaster becomes a choice, because the evidence is complete and the men who need it are standing on that deck. The report is never sent.
blocks.through_line_state: Closed again, dripping.
shots: ECU — water running off the lion's face, back into the harbour
MEDIUM lateral — Fleming and Jakobsson not looking at each other
CU high — a blank sheet of paper on the chart table, no ink on it
WIDE low — the men filing below deck, the trial over
MEDIUM high — the empty deck, level again, as if nothing happened

blocks.vo_line: The king is nine hundred kilometres away, losing a war, and writing impatient letters. Telling him his flagship cannot float is not a career move anyone wants to make.
blocks.through_line_state: A carved sample lid sits on the king's table as a paperweight, unmentioned in the letter beside it.
shots: ECU overhead — a letter being written, the words hard and fast
WIDE high — a battlefield map bristling with counters, Sweden losing ground
MEDIUM lateral — the king's silhouette against tent canvas, back to camera
CU low — the sample lion lid holding down a corner of the map, gold dulled by candle smoke
MEDIUM high — the sealed letter travelling north over grey water

blocks.vo_line: Sunday, the tenth of August, sixteen twenty-eight: Stockholm's waterfront is packed and foreign ambassadors have been invited. About one hundred and fifty people are aboard, many of them crew families.
blocks.through_line_state: Polished again for the ceremony.
shots: WIDE high — the packed waterfront, hats and banners, church towers behind
MEDIUM lateral — ambassadors in foreign dress being shown to the front
CU low — families crossing the gangplank, baskets and bundles
ECU — a cloth going over the lion lid one last time, then away
WIDE low — the ship from the water, crowded rails, everyone waving

blocks.vo_line: She is warped along the waterfront on ropes, then sets four sails. To salute the city, the gun port lids are opened and the cannon are run out.
blocks.through_line_state: OPENED — the lid swings up and is hooked back.
shots: MEDIUM low — ropes straining, the hull creeping along the quay
WIDE lateral — four sails dropping and filling in sequence
ECU — the lion lid swung upward and hooked open, daylight flooding the port
CU high — a bronze muzzle running out through the open port
WIDE high — the whole hull from above, every lower port now a black square

blocks.vo_line: Remember those gilded lion lids. They are standing wide open now, and the lower row of them sits barely one metre above the flat grey harbour water.
blocks.through_line_state: Open, one metre above the surface.
shots: ECU lateral — from inside the gun deck, the open port framing flat grey water a metre below
MEDIUM low — the deck's whole row of open ports, daylight in each one
CU overhead — the gap between port sill and sea, measured by the eye
MEDIUM lateral — the hooked-open lid seen from within, gold bright, doing nothing at all
WIDE low — the gun deck corridor, every port a bright square, water level with the sills

blocks.vo_line: She clears the sheltered water below the cliffs, and the first gust catches her sails. She heels hard, rights herself slowly, and the crowd on shore keeps cheering.
blocks.through_line_state: The lid tilts toward the surface and back.
shots: WIDE low — the ship emerging from the cliff's wind shadow
CU high — sails snapping taut all at once
ECU — the open lid swinging down toward the water, then lifting away
MEDIUM lateral — the crowd on shore, still cheering, seeing nothing wrong
WIDE high — the ship righting, mast describing a slow arc against cloud

blocks.vo_line: The second gust is not stronger, and it does not need to be. She lies over onto her side, and the open lower gun ports go under the waterline.
blocks.through_line_state: Goes under.
shots: MEDIUM low — the second gust arriving as a dark line across the water
WIDE lateral — the hull laying over, decks tipping toward vertical
ECU — the open lion lid meeting the surface and passing through it
CU high — the sea pouring over the port sill in a smooth sheet
WIDE high — the ship on her side, sails flat on the water

blocks.vo_line: Water enters through the lion mouths and runs downhill to the low side. That makes her lean further, which opens the next port, and lets still more sea inside.
blocks.through_line_state: Water pours through the lion's open mouth.
shots: ECU lateral — water surging through the lion-mouthed port, gold under green
WIDE low — the gun deck tilting, water sheeting across it
CU high — a cannon breaking its lashings and sliding downhill
MEDIUM lateral — the gun crew scrambling upslope, hands on beams
WIDE high — a cutaway of the hull, the loop drawn plainly: in, down, over, in

blocks.vo_line: That loop has no exit. The most expensive object in Sweden goes down within twenty minutes, thirteen hundred metres from where she started, taking roughly thirty people with her.
blocks.through_line_state: The lid sinks past, still hooked open.
shots: WIDE high — the ship settling, masts still above water, sails soaked flat
MEDIUM lateral — small boats rowing hard from the shore
ECU — the hooked-open lid sliding down past camera into the dark
CU high — the last mast tip going under, water closing over it
WIDE low — flat water, floating debris, thirteen hundred metres of harbour behind

blocks.vo_line: The inquest is immediate and furious. Officers blame the shipwrights, who point at a specification nobody is willing to question, because it came from the king himself.
blocks.through_line_state: A salvaged lid leans against the chamber wall as evidence nobody examines.
shots: MEDIUM lateral — an inquest chamber, officers seated in a hard row
CU low — the surviving captain answering, hands flat on the table
ECU overhead — a clerk's page, names listed, one column left blank
MEDIUM high — the waterlogged lion lid propped against the panelling, unlooked at
WIDE high — the chamber from above, everyone pointing somewhere else

blocks.vo_line: Nobody is punished, and the verdict records only that the ship was badly proportioned and that God permitted it. The stability trial appears nowhere in the written account.
blocks.through_line_state: Carried out of the room and left in the dark, still unrecorded.
shots: ECU overhead — the verdict written out, short, final
MEDIUM lateral — the record book closing
CU high — the shelf it is filed onto, among identical spines
MEDIUM low — the lion lid carried out through a doorway and set down in an unlit passage
WIDE low — the empty chamber after everyone has left, one candle guttering

blocks.vo_line: Then the Baltic does something strange: its water is far too cold and fresh for the shipworm that devours wooden wrecks everywhere else. So she does not rot at all, only waits.
blocks.through_line_state: Silt-sealed and intact — preserved by the thing that drowned her.
shots: WIDE high — the wreck settling into silt, light failing above
ECU — the lion lid going grey under a slow fall of sediment
CU lateral — timber grain intact under a thin skin of mud
MEDIUM low — the hull whole in the dark, decks still standing
WIDE lateral — three centuries compressed: silt deepening, seasons passing above

blocks.vo_line: On the twenty-fourth of April, nineteen sixty-one, she breaks the surface again after three hundred and thirty-three years. Over ninety-eight percent of her timber is original, lion lids included.
blocks.through_line_state: Lifted, streaming water, the gold still legible.
shots: WIDE low — cables coming taut between pontoons, water boiling
MEDIUM lateral — the black hull breaking the surface, mud sheeting off
ECU — the lion lid clearing the water, gold showing through silt
CU high — press boats and cameras crowding the cordon
WIDE high — the whole wreck afloat again, dwarfing the barges around it

blocks.vo_line: She now has her own museum and draws a million visitors a year, more than any warship that won a battle. The silence cost thirty lives and bought four centuries of fame.
blocks.through_line_state: Under museum glass, lit and labelled — the object that sank her, preserved.
shots: WIDE low — the ship in a dim hall, lit from below, five storeys of it
MEDIUM lateral — visitors on walkways, tiny against the hull
ECU — the lion lid behind glass, gold still readable, a label beneath it
CU high — a row of gun ports, all closed now, from the top gallery
WIDE high — the hall from above, the crowd flowing around the hull
